service.description: A party as the current user may see it (the entity filters, and a personal contact only its owner's) and what the user may do with it. With need (view, edit or delete) an error when the user may not; a party the user may not see is "not found".

parameter.name: need
parameter.description: view, edit or delete; empty only reports

service.description: The side list rows of the parties given, in their order, leaving out those the user may not see and the disabled (merged or deleted) ones: name, kind, organization and title (a person's current PrtContact or PrtEmployee relationship to an organization the user may see), the primary email (EmailPrimary first) and phone (PhonePrimary, then PhoneMobile, first), personal or not, a face image or not, and the star of the user's default book.

The Contacts side list for a scope, narrowed by text (name, organization, email or phone), a group of a book and a first letter, limited (a 320 px pane has no room for paging): all (the directory and the user's personal contacts, mantle.party.PartyServices.find#Party), directory (find#Party without personal contacts), mine (the members of the user's personal books and the user's personal contacts), a contact book id (find#ContactBookParties, with contactBookGroupId), recent (the parties of the user's communication events of the last 90 days, the latest first) and ungrouped (the members of the user's books that are in no group of them). The rows are get#ContactRows'. The scope's book, its groups and the user's books come back for the scope selector and the chips.

parameter.name: rowCount
parameter.description: The rows found, maybe more than shown

parameter.name: contactBook
parameter.description: The book of a book scope, from get#UserContactBooks

service.description: What the contact record shows of a party the user may see (check#ContactAccess), for template/ContactRecord.xml: the names, the access, the roles, the contact information other than addresses with their purposes (the expired ones too with showExpired), the addresses, a person's organizations and titles, the relationships, the books and groups the party is in among the user's books, the notes, the employee directory card (organization, position, manager), and for a personal contact the books of its banner. Nothing for a party the user may not see.

parameter.name: otherBookList
parameter.description: The user's books the party is not in that the user may edit

service.description: One tab of the contact record beyond the overview, for a party the user may see: calendar (the party's events from 30 days ago to 90 days ahead, mantle.work.EventServices.get#FullCalendarData), tasks (the WetTask work efforts the party is on, open ones first), requests (the requests the party is on) and consent (mantle.party.ConsentServices.get#PartyConsentState, read only).

The names of a contact the user may change (mantle.party.PartyServices.update#PartyDetail); a field left out is not changed, an empty one is cleared. A person needs a first or last name, an organization a name.

A person's organization and title: with partyRelationshipId the title (relationshipName) of that current PrtContact or PrtEmployee relationship; with organizationPartyId (an organization the user may see) a new PrtContact relationship, or the title of the current one to it. thruNow ends the relationship given.

A relationship of a contact the user may change to another party the user may see: the contact is the from party (the type describes it: Joe is a Contact of Acme) unless reverse; a directory party is not related to a personal contact.
A note on a contact the user may change (mantle.party.PartyNote); with noteDate the user's own note of that date is changed, or removed when noteText is empty.

An email, phone, website or address of a contact the user may change, with its purpose: new, or with contactMechId a change of that one (mantle.party.ContactServices.store#PartyContactInfo, which keeps the purpose and makes a new contact mechanism for the changed value). kind is email, phone, web or postal; a phone is digits, ten of them an area code and number, eleven starting with 1 also the country code, or countryCode, areaCode and contactNumber as given.

Adds a purpose to a current contact mechanism of a contact the user may change (store#PartyContactMech), or with remove ends that purpose (delete#PartyContactMech); without a purpose remove ends the contact mechanism.
The face image of a contact the user may change (mantle.party.PartyServices.create#PartyContent with PcntFaceImage); an image file only.
The location of the latest face image of a party the user may see; null when it has none.

Puts a contact the user may see in a book the user may edit, with the groups of that book given (and out of the book's other groups), or with remove takes it out of the book (mantle.party.ContactBookServices add#ContactBookParties, remove#ContactBookGroupParties and remove#ContactBookParties check the book's permission and that a personal contact goes only in its owner's books).

Deletes contacts the user may delete (check#ContactAccess need delete): the party is disabled and its book memberships end (the user's personal contact, or a directory party for a contact admin). Each contact on its own: one that cannot be deleted is named in failedPartyIdList with the reason as a warning, and the rest are deleted.

The contacts given (those the user may see) or a book the user may view (with its group) as a vCard or CSV file (mantle.party.ContactImportServices.export#Contacts), written to the user's own export folder, dbresource://ironstone/ContactExport/{userId}/, for the screen to send as a download (ec.web.sendResourceResponse, which names the file from the location).

Two contacts side by side for a merge (both must be ones the user may see and change): the fields each has, the rows of the compare (label, the two values, and which differ), and whether they may be merged and which way: a directory party is never merged into a personal contact (link the personal contact to the directory instead), and an internal organization is never merged away.

Merges one contact into the other the user keeps (get#ComparePair says which may be kept): the fields chosen from the other side first go on the kept one (update#PartyDetail), then mantle.party.DuplicateServices.merge#Parties moves the rest (contact information, roles, relationships, books, groups, work efforts, requests, messages) and disables the other party. A personal contact merged into a directory party is linked to the directory (link#PersonalContactToDirectory).

parameter.name: takeFields
parameter.description: Comma-separated fields to take from the other contact

service.description: The candidate duplicate pairs the last scan found (parties with hasDuplicates Y, mantle.party.DuplicateServices find#PartyDuplicates for their matches), among the directory parties the user may see (the duplicate services leave personal contacts out, and they are left out here too), without the pairs marked not duplicates (the PartySetting BossNotDuplicates of either party, a comma list of party ids), grouped by reason: same email, same phone, same name (a person's first and last name and birthday, or an organization's name), same address and same identification. The name pass is BOSS's: find#PartyDuplicates matches a name only with a birthday.

Records that two directory parties the user may see are not duplicates (contact admins only): each party's PartySetting BossNotDuplicates lists the other, so get#DuplicatePairs leaves the pair out, and the parties' duplicate flags clear. Mantle has no record of this yet (the next scan flags the parties again; the setting keeps the pair out of the list).
The draft of an import of the current user: the draft map (empty when there is none, or the id is not a draft id), the location of its file, and the folder.

actions.script: draft = {} found = false fileLocation = null const userId = ec.user.userId if (!userId || !importId || !/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}$/.test(String(importId))) return folder = `dbresource://ironstone/ContactImport/${userId}/${importId}` const text = ec.resource.getLocationReference(folder + '/draft.json').getText() if (!text) return try { draft = JSON.parse(text) || {} } catch (err) { ec.logger.warn(`Contact import ${importId} of ${userId}: the draft does not read: ${err}`); draft = {}; return } found = true fileLocation = draft.fileExt ? `${folder}/source.${draft.fileExt}` : null

service.description: Merges the fields given into the draft of an import of the current user and saves it.

The import's first step: the file (an upload, or the file already in the draft when none is given) read as text in its character set (UTF-8, Windows-1252, ISO-8859-1 or UTF-16 with its byte order mark; the framework's FileItem.getString reads UTF-8 only), kept as the draft's source file, and parsed (mantle.party.ContactImportServices.parse#ContactFile) for its kind, preset, columns and mapping, which start the draft. A new import gets an id; the same importId replaces its file.

The import's last step: mantle.party.ContactImportServices.import#Contacts of the draft's file with its mapping and options (each row in its own transaction: a row that fails is reported and the rest are imported), the result kept in the draft (counts, the failures with their reasons and values, the rows) for the result view and the failures download. A directory import is for contact admins.
